summary.headline: Captain Polyplast Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 9.66% (from 10.29%) on HDPE/LLDPE cost spike; solar pump order intake reached INR82.4 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 32.89% YoY to INR106.43 crore, with EBITDA up 24.75% to INR10.28 crore and net profit up 5.55% to INR4.48 crore. Margin compression came from sharp year-on-year increases in HDPE and LLDPE costs in micro-irrigation, while higher working capital needs raised interest cost in H1. Management expects benchmark cost revisions for micro-irrigation and Ahmedabad plant ramp-up to restore margins in H2. Solar pump order wins were the highlight, including the largest single solar EPC order in company history.

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR89 crore, of which INR77.72 crore due within 1 year

segments.name: Solar EPC / solar pumps (PM-KUSUM)
segments.commentary: Two repeat MSEDCL orders won in Q2: INR23.6 crore for 1,000 pumps (July) and INR47 crore for 2,000 pumps (September). FY27 order intake reached INR82.4 crore for 3,500 pumps; cumulative orders since Maharashtra empanelment in August 2025 total 5,000 pumps. Segment EBITDA margin about 10-11%.

segments.name: Micro-irrigation
segments.commentary: Margin compressed to about 7-8% on petrochemical raw material (HDPE, LLDPE) cost increases. Subsidy programmes account for roughly 90% of market; commercial and export sales are about 10% of the micro-irrigation mix.

guidance_outlook: Benchmark cost revision for micro-irrigation from central and state governments expected in coming months (management said probably Q3); management expects at least 1 percentage point EBITDA margin uplift once effective, with pass-through of raw material costs.
Ahmedabad facility ramp-up expected to add about 0.5 percentage point to EBITDA margin by March 2027; full 1-1.5 percentage point benefit from in-house manufacturing expected over about 3 years.
Majority of INR82.4 crore solar pump order revenue expected to be recognised before end of Q3 FY27; further tenders to be recognised in Q4 as won.
Micro-irrigation working capital cycle (currently about 8 months) expected to fall by end of March 2027; solar pump cycle 3-4 months; consolidated cycle expected at 5-6 months at FY27 end.
Further solar pump opportunities expected beyond Maharashtra once PM-KUSUM phase 2 is announced; no fresh tendering in other states in FY27 so far.
Management said profit growth should move in line with revenue growth in H2 FY27 if benchmark revision takes effect.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad manufacturing facility began production in the last quarter (Q1 FY27 per Q&A); ramp-up in phases, with some components (currently outsourced) being made in-house.
Automation solutions for drip irrigation launched last year; scope expanding to time-based and volume-based irrigation control.
No capex quantum or capacity utilisation figures disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Water conservation and El Nino-driven deficient monsoon are raising micro-irrigation demand in certain pockets; state governments reportedly reviving micro-irrigation focus.
PM-KUSUM 1 deadline extended from March 2026; no fresh tendering in states beyond Maharashtra this year; PM-KUSUM 2 expected soon.
Pricing: management said raw material price increases were not yet passed through; pass-through depends on government benchmark revision, amount not yet known.
Non-subsidy/commercial and export sales (about 10% of micro-irrigation mix) are being prioritised; they are small relative to subsidy market.
Receivables are largely from government agencies; management says recovery risk is minimal, though H1 receivables are seasonally high.

qa_highlights.question: How is execution of the INR82.4 crore solar pump order book progressing and when will revenue be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution is ongoing and much revenue was recognised in Q1 and Q2; the remainder is expected by Q3, with new tender wins recognised in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made in states beyond Maharashtra, such as Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Haryana?
qa_highlights.answer: No fresh tendering in those states this year because the PM-KUSUM 1 deadline was extended; empanelment is expected after PM-KUSUM 2 is announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT grow much slower than revenue in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material cost increases compressed micro-irrigation margins and higher working capital raised H1 interest cost; H1 EBITDA margin was roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle target and cash release potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation cycle is 8 months, expected to fall by March; solar pumps 3-4 months; consolidated cycle expected at 5-6 months at year end. No cash-release quantum given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage INR77.72 crore of borrowings due within one year?
qa_highlights.answer: Most debt is revolving working capital borrowing renewed annually; actual annual repayments are under INR10 crore and manageable from accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medium-term EBITDA margin, ROCE and ROE targets, and levers?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric medium-term targets given. Levers are benchmark cost revision (at least 1 percentage point, outside management control) and Ahmedabad ramp-up (0.5 percentage point by March).

qa_highlights.question: Why are significant receivables still outstanding though classified as not yet due?
qa_highlights.answer: Most receivables are from government agencies under subsidy programmes; management says recovery risk is minimal and receivables are typically collected when state funds are released, mainly in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the contingent liability increase to INR15.20 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly performance bank guarantees, which governments typically demand at about 1% of sales, plus 5-year warranties on micro-irrigation systems. No specific legal claims were described.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margins of solar EPC versus micro-irrigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins were similar last year; now micro-irrigation is about 7-8% and solar pumps about 10-11%.

risks_watch: Raw material (HDPE/LLDPE) price pressure persists if benchmark cost revision is delayed or smaller than hoped; management could not quantify the revision.
Working capital intensity and rising borrowings (INR89 crore FY26, INR77.72 crore short-term) with H1 receivables seasonally high; collection timing depends on state government fund release.
Solar pump growth outside Maharashtra depends on PM-KUSUM 2 announcement and new tenders, timing not confirmed.
Concentration of revenue in government subsidy programmes (about 90% of micro-irrigation market).
Contingent liabilities rose to INR15.20 crore in FY26; management gave no specifics on claims or legal status.
Monitor Q3 FY27 for benchmark revision outcome and Ahmedabad ramp-up contribution to margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on solar pump order momentum and margin recovery levers, but cautious and somewhat evasive on quantification: benchmark price revision size and timing, medium-term margin/ROCE/ROE targets, and specifics of contingent liabilities and promoter loans were not answered in numbers.
key_quotes: The order was the largest ever single solar EPC order win for the company in its history.

The EBITDA margin for the quarter declined year -on-year. This decline was primarily due to the sharp increase in the raw material costs, especially costs for HDPE and LLDPE compared to the last year.
So the first one I cannot calculate at this point or I cannot comment on at this point how much price increase would be accepted by the government.

adds.what: Ahmedabad manufacturing facility (in-house components, phased ramp-up)

growth.why: Q2 revenue (total income) grew 32.89% and EBITDA 24.75%, with H1 revenue up 25.14%; management guides H2 profit to track revenue growth if the benchmark micro-irrigation price revision lands (at least 1pp margin uplift, probably Q3), plus 0.5pp from Ahmedabad by March 2027, backed by INR82.4 crore solar pump orders but with the price revision amount not yet known.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects at least 1pp EBITDA margin uplift from benchmark micro-irrigation cost revision (probably Q3) plus about 0.5pp from Ahmedabad by March 2027, against a Q2 margin that fell to 9.66% from 10.29%; revision size not yet quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (already live), ramping through FY27
rows.why: Ahmedabad facility began production in Q1 FY27 with phased ramp-up and some outsourced components moving in-house; no new capacity figures disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Solar pump order intake reached INR82.4 crore for 3,500 pumps in FY27 (cumulative 5,000 pumps since Maharashtra empanelment), with H1 revenue up 25.14% YoY; the majority of the order revenue is due by Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex quantum or utilisation figure was disclosed, and the Ahmedabad plant is already commissioned, so there is no stated plan for a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says H2 profit growth should track revenue growth (H1 revenue +25.14% vs H1 PAT +7%) if the benchmark revision takes effect, but the revision size is unknown.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material cost pressure is unpassed, and management could not quantify the benchmark revision, so a delay or smaller revision would keep micro-irrigation margins at about 7-8%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Automation solutions for drip irrigation were launched last year and are expanding to time-based and volume-based control, but no dated launch was given.

rows.label: PM-KUSUM 2 announcement enabling new state solar pump tenders
rows.why: No fresh tendering outside Maharashtra in FY27 so far, and management expects empanelment in other states only after PM-KUSUM 2 is announced; timing not confirmed.

rows.label: Working capital cycle falls to 5-6 months
rows.why: Micro-irrigation cycle (about 8 months) is expected to fall by March 2027 and the consolidated cycle is guided to 5-6 months, though no cash-release quantum was given against INR77.72 crore of short-term borrowings.

rows.label: Micro-irrigation benchmark cost revision (pass-through of HDPE/LLDPE)
rows.why: Management expects the government benchmark revision probably in Q3 with at least 1pp EBITDA margin uplift, but the amount is not yet known and micro-irrigation margins are about 7-8%.

tone.note: Management was confident on solar pump order momentum and the benchmark revision and Ahmedabad margin levers, but cautious and evasive on quantification of the revision, medium-term targets and contingent liabilities; analysts pushed on margin compression, working capital and borrowings.
